final_answer:
Let
\[
D=\Delta=v^2+uw.
\]
From the definitions,
\[
q^2+pr=(v+wD)^2+w(u-2vD-wD^2)=v^2+uw=D.
\]
Also
\[
w=r,\qquad v=q-r(q^2+pr),\qquad u=p+2q(q^2+pr)-r(q^2+pr)^2.
\]
Hence \(A=k[p,q,r]\).

Now set
\[
\xi=p+q,\qquad \eta=q+r,\qquad \zeta=r.
\]
Then \(A=k[\xi,\eta,\zeta]\). In these coordinates, \(\sigma\) and \(\tau\) are diagonal. Indeed,
\[
\sigma(\xi)=P+Q=-8(p+q)=-8\xi,
\]
\[
\sigma(\eta)=Q+R=-27(q+r)=-27\eta,
\]
\[
\sigma(\zeta)=R=-125\zeta,
\]
and similarly
\[
\tau(\xi)=\widetilde P+\widetilde Q=-\frac14\xi,\qquad
\tau(\eta)=\widetilde Q+\widetilde R=-\frac19\eta,\qquad
\tau(\zeta)=\widetilde R=-\frac1{25}\zeta.
\]

Every element of \(R\) has a unique finite normal form
\[
\sum a_{i,j,m,n}x^i y^j z^m t^n,\qquad a_{i,j,m,n}\in A.
\]
The monomial \(x^i y^j z^m t^n\) acts on \(A\) by
\[
\sigma^{i-j}\tau^{m-n}.
\]
For it to commute with all of \(A\), we need
\[
\sigma^{i-j}\tau^{m-n}=\mathrm{id}.
\]
Writing
\[
a=i-j,\qquad b=m-n,
\]
this requires, on \(\xi,\eta,\zeta\),
\[
(-8)^a\left(-\frac14\right)^b=1,\qquad
(-27)^a\left(-\frac19\right)^b=1,\qquad
(-125)^a\left(-\frac1{25}\right)^b=1.
\]
Thus
\[
3a-2b=0
\]
and the sign condition gives \(a+b\) even. Hence
\[
(a,b)=(4s,6s),\qquad s\in\mathbb Z.
\]

So the central monomials are exactly products generated by
\[
xy,\qquad zt,\qquad x^4z^6,\qquad y^4t^6.
\]
Their coefficients must lie in
\[
A^{\langle\sigma,\tau\rangle}=k,
\]
because a monomial \(\xi^\alpha\eta^\beta\zeta^\gamma\) fixed by \(\sigma\) must satisfy
\[
(-8)^\alpha(-27)^\beta(-125)^\gamma=1,
\]
forcing \(\alpha=\beta=\gamma=0\).

Therefore
\[
\boxed{Z(R)=k[\,xy,\ zt,\ x^4z^6,\ y^4t^6\,]}.
\]

These generators satisfy the internal relation
\[
(x^4z^6)(y^4t^6)=(xy)^4(zt)^6,
\]
but as a subalgebra of \(R\), the displayed generated algebra is the explicit center.
